convention: e^{jωt}; ε_r = ε′ − jε″; φ = 0 is the bearing from the stem's axis through the node

outputs.field_same_current_dB: |F(φ)|² — the far field with the tree against the same source current without it; EXACT in the horizontal plane for a short dipole (TM) or small loop (TE) along an infinite stem (k_z = 0)
outputs.gain_dB: |F(φ)|²/(P_in/P₀) — the same field at equal INPUT power; 2-D normalisation, an indicator
outputs.efficiency: P_rad/P_in in 2-D — an indicator of the near-field loss, not the 3-D antenna efficiency

verdict: In the horizontal plane, with the gateway straight behind the stem the field of a short dipole along the stem (TM) is 10.6–34.5 dB below its level with the gateway in front, and its deepest null lies 13.4–54.4 dB below the front at 138.25–180.0° from it; at 90° it is 6.1–9.7 dB down, and it stays within 3 dB of the front only to 53–66°. A dipole tangential to the bark (TE, horizontal E): 7.7–48.0 dB behind, 9.2–21.1 dB at 90°. Ranges span every NAMED reading of the stem's permittivity, diameter and the antenna's standoff in this cache; over the sapwood width's measured axis (2.2–13.6 cm, the width sweep — the output is resonant in the width) the TM 3-dB sector runs 52–71°, the TM loss at 90° reaches 10.3 dB, and the back spans 10.2–54.9 dB (TM) and 7.7–71.1 dB (TE). Over the stem's diameter as an axis too (38–60 cm in 1 cm steps, the bark derived per stem, every width, bark and standoff) the TM 3-dB sector's floor is 50° on the 1° grid (the −3 dB crossing ≥ 50.35°), so the ratified ±50° rule holds on that grid with a margin of 0.35° on the crossing; the TM floor behind on that grid is 10.2 dB. The dead bark is the third resonant axis: swept from canon's thin to thick end (1 mm steps) on the TM «phloem» stem the sector's floor is 49° (crossing ≥ 49.85°, at DBH 54 cm, bark 30.8 mm, sapwood 2.4 cm), so the ±50° rule FAILS on the 1° grid over the bark axis (first failing stem 54 cm); under the dry and wet proxies the floor is 54° at the thin end and 57° at the thick end; the loss at ±50° on the crossing-floor row is 3.018 dB (3.014–3.033 over the A.36 readings), a deck 1.0 mm higher returns the rule, and past the thick end the crossing keeps falling (the floor is an edge of the table). Past the bark table (stems to 90 cm, three bark assumptions) the rule — thin end held: first fails at 86 cm; thin end slope: first fails at 76 cm; thick end slope: holds to 90 cm. The 2-D efficiency indicator — what the near field loses into the stem — is 0.13–0.70 (TM) and 0.15–0.54 (TE); it is not the 3-D antenna efficiency.
